data.text/markdown:
Sampling, convergence and performance

Compare PXR/CBS yields for six fixed-history budgets and one adaptive stopping policy. All runs use a 30 keV beam, 100 nm HOPG, 135° observation, and no bremsstrahlung. The 600–2,000 eV band integral is less noisy than individual grid samples. Small CPU budgets illustrate the method, not validated precision; sampled histories are not physical bunch charge.

Adaptive stopping

AdaptiveSampling monitors the per-electron relative standard error (RSE) of the selected CXR band contribution, with additional maximum-share, effective-sample-size and stability guards. This is not an RSE estimate for each photon-energy bin. A run can reach its maximum without convergence. block_electrons determines how often stopping is checked; cxr_chunk separately controls the spectrum-reduction kernel. The loose RSE target is illustrative, and the default safeguards remain enabled.

data.text/markdown:
Interpretation

The largest fixed-budget yield is only a reference, not ground truth. Both modes use the default seed 1, the same per-electron CPU core, the same CXR spectrum chunk size, and equal CXR/bremsstrahlung transport populations. Those choices matter even with bremsstrahlung scoring disabled: the second population affects transport energy cutoffs. Fixed-budget points share random draws, so their spread is not an independent-sample uncertainty. Check stop_reason, statistics_limited, the measured RSE, and every entry in guard_passes before calling an adaptive run converged. The requested case["Ne"] remains its maximum, for provenance and cache identity; the plotted count is realized_electrons. The stopping monitor measures per-electron CXR mass, whereas the plot integrates the final gridded spectral density. Changing reflection families or photon grids tests systematic discretization, not sampling convergence. Wall times depend on compilation, caching and hardware. The untimed warmup helps, but these are not portable benchmarks. These runs do not estimate uncertainty across independent seeds. Use transport_core="cuda" consistently for GPU comparisons. Try increasing the budgets and compare the sampling reference and performance guidance.
